text:
raj: heads-up — hitting strange fragmentation OOMs running AWQ-quantized lumen12b on our 2xA100 Triton pool. vLLM path doesn't OOM but has huge tail latency spikes after ~2000 requests :thinking_face:
emma: can you paste the exact error/logs? Triton version + driver?
raj: error snippet: `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 3.20 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total, 35.10 GiB free)` then a bunch of cudaMalloc retries. driver: 535.86, container base: pytorch-nightly + cuda 12.1 image.
yun: is this reproducible with single request sequence or only sustained traffic?
raj: reproduces on single long prompt too — appears after a few prefix tokens when KV cache grows. On Triton we see fragmentation grow over warmup. vLLM uses a single long-lived allocation path, so avoids fragmentation but latency variance is bad.
marta: can you share Triton model config? instance_group and dynamic_batching?
raj: config excerpt: ```
model_config:
  instance_group:
    count: 2
    kind: KIND_GPU
  dynamic_batching: true
  instance_count: 1
  parameters:
    GPU_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB: 0
```
oliver: two quick asks: 1) try PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128,garbage_collection_threshold:0.6 2) set TRITON server env TRITON_SERVER_GPU_ALLOCATOR=cuda_async? we had fragmentation fixes with async allocator on some kernels.
ym: (typo) sorry yun.
raj: tried PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF — reduced frequency but still stray OOMs on certain seq lengths. Tried CUDA_MALLOC_ASYNC_WORKSPACE_SIZE=0.5GB — less fragmentation but performance worse.
emma: could be allocator vs Tensorrt backend differences. Are you using TensorRT-LLM plugin for the int8 path or native TRITON/PyTorch path?
raj: this run uses TRT-LLM for final kernels (INT8 AWQ) — plugin exposes custom alloc hooks. vLLM run uses torch-indirect path (no TRT). That difference aligns with behavior.
marta: request we do a small repro harness: script that runs increasing sequence length and prints free memory between tokens. We should also capture `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.free,memory.used --format=csv` periodically and `cuda-memcheck` logs.
raj: wrote a quick repro and kicked a CI job: job/4872 (ci-bot: https://ci.redwood/job/4872). It runs on the Triton pool with 2xA100.
ci-bot: job/4872 started on pool-triton-2xa100 (container: rl-inference:v2026-03c). Logs: https://ci.redwood/job/4872/logs
yun: small theory: TRT-LLM's custom allocator fragments when mixing small KV allocations with large kernel scratch buffers; async allocator tries to defragment but won't free pinned host pages. Could be pinned mem vs device mem mixing.
oliver: try disabling TRT-LLM scratch reuse: set TRTLLM_DISABLE_SCRATCH_REUSE=1 and rerun. Also try setting TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=0 (if enabled).
raj: run with TRTLLM_DISABLE_SCRATCH_REUSE=1 — initial run survived longer but still OOM at high seq. attaching small log: `allocated blocks: [ 64MiB, 1GiB, 256MiB, 512MiB ]` gaps appear.
emma: if it's allocator fragmentation, we can try 1) force single allocation for KV cache via runtime flag (pre-allocate max_kv_size) 2) adjust Triton instance_group to 1 instance per GPU to reduce multiple CUDA contexts.
marta: note: for Dedicated pool we pin one model instance per GPU (was helpful for Mistral runs). Try instance_group.count: 1 and instance_count: 1 per GPU.
yun: also check cudnn/cublas workspace growth — some TensorRT kernels request huge scratch temporarily which can produce hole when freed. TRT sometimes returns memory to system in a non-contiguous way.
\araj: (typo, meant raj) updated run: instance_group single instance, TRTLLM_DISABLE_SCRATCH_REUSE=1, PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF set. Run lasted 3x longer no OOM. Latency tail still worse than vLLM but acceptable.
emma: can we capture allocator histograms next? nvprof isn't great for this but `cudaMalloc` tracing or `cuda-memcheck --leak-check full` might help. Also check driver warnings in dmesg — fragmentation sometimes causes driver kill/recovery.
raj: no driver recoveries, clean. nvml shows increasing fragmentation metric (?) — we'll collect PGIs.
oliver: long-term we should add a Triton backend shim that prefers large contiguous allocations for KV cache (reserve_max_kv_mb). Filing infra ticket to add config knob.
emma: filing infra ticket INF-1229 to add reserve_max_kv_mb and allocator histograms. tagging @infra-bot. :clipboard:
infra-bot: ticket INF-1229 created and assigned to eng-infra.
raj: quick workaround notes for runbook: 1) prefer vLLM path when latency tails aren't critical 2) for Triton+TRT-LLM set single instance per GPU + TRTLLM_DISABLE_SCRATCH_REUSE + PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF 3) pre-allocate KV with runtime flag if supported. I'll add to model onboarding checklist. :white_check_mark:
emma: great — can you add the small repro script to the model onboarding tests repo so new models get smoke-tested?
raj: will open PR after CI passes. thanks all. :pray:
